_: What the control room looks like (dev-docs/poltergeist/control-room.md, 3.5).
This file is data. tools/gen-control-room-look.py turns it into
tools/the-control-room-look-is-one-set.py is red when either is out of step.
Lengths are points, times are seconds. These are readings off the design, not off a product.
Every value names where it was read (`src`, a key of `sources`); a group's `_src` covers the
values in it that name none. A value the user has not ruled on carries `tentative`, with the
other candidate, so that ruling on it is one edit here and both hosts follow.
A colour is `#RRGGBB`, or `#RRGGBB@a` with a from 0 to 1.

font._doc: Type sizes. Nothing is set smaller than `min`.

body.doc: Body text, tab titles, the terminal.

group_name.doc: A group's name in the list.

weight_emphasis.doc: The selected tab, a status word, a title.

line._doc: The only two widths there are.

stroke.doc: The plus and the cross; the rail of the time band.

window.doc: The system's; drawn as 14 in the design.

row.doc: 12 = 6 + 6: concentric with the panel through its padding.

supervisor_inner.doc: The terminal inside the supervisor's frame: 12 - 4.

worker.doc: 8 until v15: everything 8 from the window's edge is 12.

window_edge.doc: From the window's edge to anything.

supervisor_bezel.doc: The supervisor's border, and its gap to the terminal inside.

terminal_text_inset.doc: Left and right of the terminal's text.

window_tab._doc: A window tab holds three things: close, title, one status glyph.

side_slot.doc: The width kept on each side, so the title stays centred.

working_glyph_shown.doc: Whether a working terminal's spinner is drawn on a window tab. Off, so that every glyph in the row of tabs is one to look at.

tentative.why: The design drew it; the supervisor chose not to. The user has not ruled.

width.doc: Wide enough that what a row waits on is 322 across: 41 characters of the terminal's face, which is one step of most commands. The user, 2026-10-13: "A is better, it can be wider".

quiet_row_height.doc: A group that needs nothing: one line.

separator_space_above.doc: Below the last waiting row's own gap.

row_line1_height.doc: The glyph, the name, who is waiting and the status word. A waiting row is this, then its lines of what it waits on, inside `row_padding_y` above and below: 60, 80 or 100 high for one, two or three lines.

ask_line_height.doc: One line of what a row waits on.

fix_line_height.doc: The line under a card that reads Failed, holding its Fix button (task 1560) and, when the last press was refused, why: a regular-size push button at the menu's font, which does not fit in `ask_line_height`.

tentative.why: Not in the design. 28 is the room the retention notice's OK takes; 24 would fit a small button, whose font is under the menu's.

ask_max_lines.doc: How many lines what a row waits on may wrap to. A sentence takes up to this many and ends in an ellipsis. A command of this many steps or fewer gives every step a line first, and what is left over to the steps that need a second.

tentative.why: The design's direction B drew four. The user chose A, which draws three.

ask_max_steps.doc: A command of more steps than `ask_max_lines` is not cut to that many lines: every step keeps one line, cut at its end, so the start of every step shows. Past this many the last line says how many steps are not shown, rather than dropping them without a word.

tentative.why: 3 is the design's cap applied to steps as well, which hides the fourth step of a command behind an ellipsis -- the step that may be the dangerous one. The supervisor ruled that out; where the ceiling is, nobody has.

ask_cells_per_line.doc: How many characters of the terminal's face one line of what a row waits on holds: the count a host uses when it has no font to measure with. A wide character is two.

status_word_gap.doc: Between a glyph and its word.

mark_gap.doc: Between a group's pinned mark and its muted mark, to the right of its name (task 1660). From the name to the first mark is `row_item_gap`; each mark is `glyph` square.

group_note._doc: The group's note, edited in a panel docked at the window's right (tasks 1660, 1661; design v21 `04-B`, the user's choice of 2026-10-16). The supervisor's frame gives up the panel's width and `space.between_frames`.

feedback_seconds.doc: How long the line under a row that says the supervisor was asked (`report progress`, `close idle workers`) stays before it folds away. One that says it was not delivered stays.

pane._doc: The three frames a split can wear.

name_role_gap.doc: Between a pane's name and the word for what it is. Measured 9 to 10 between the ink; the boxes are 8 apart.

plain_title_inset_x.doc: An ordinary terminal's title, from its pane's left edge. Measured: ink at 13.

plain_title_band_height.doc: The title is centred in a band this high at the top of the pane, with nothing drawn behind it. Measured: ink from 9 to 22 below the pane's top.

supervisor_floats.doc: It has a shadow; the other two do not.

supervisor_badge._doc: The badge at the left end of a supervisor's title, the mark before a supervisor's name on a stack's tab, and the edge round a supervisor's pane when panes wear no frames (task 1692).

height.doc: Round at both ends: its radius is half of this.

padding_leading.doc: From the badge's left end to the mark.

padding_trailing.doc: From the word to the badge's right end.

mark_word_gap.doc: Between the mark and the word inside the badge. The mark is `side.glyph` square.

edge.doc: The edge drawn just inside a supervisor's pane when `poltergeist-pane-frames` is off.

tab_dots._doc: The dots on a window tab, one per pane given a colour, led by the supervisor's flag (task 1699). Columns of two, top then bottom, left to right, in the panes' reading order.

gap.doc: Between two dots, across and down: two rows are dot + gap + dot = `window_tab.glyph`.

shown_when_over.doc: With more than `max`, this many are drawn and a `+N` for the rest.

flag_gap.doc: Between the flag (`window_tab.glyph` square) and the first column.

plus_gap.doc: Between the last column and `+N`, written at `font.min` in `text_secondary`.

ring.doc: The width of the accent ring round the dots while a pane of the tab is lit (`terminal_highlight`).

ring_gap.doc: From the dots' outer edge to the ring. With no dots the ring goes round the room of one.

project_mark._doc: The mark of a page of a project: two stacked pages in a `window_tab.glyph` square, outlined in the project's colour and lit by a glow of it laid on with screen, which never makes the tab darker (task 1796).

back_x0.doc: The back page's left edge, from the square's left.

back_y0.doc: The back page's top edge, from the square's top.

front_x0.doc: The front page. The back page is drawn only where the front one is not, `front_clear` round it.

front_clear.doc: How far outside the front page the back page's line stops.

glow_radius.doc: The glow's circle, round the square's centre, before it is blurred.

glow_strength.doc: The glow's coverage at its middle, times the state's strength.

glow_blur.doc: The Gaussian blur of the glow's coverage (its sigma). Only the coverage is blurred; its colour is the project's everywhere.

core_gap.doc: Round the mark's square, the room the glow mostly stays out of, so the lines keep the tab's ground beside them.

core_radius.doc: The clear core's corner radius: the pages' 3 and `core_gap` more.

core_blur.doc: The blur of the clear core's edge.

core_keep.doc: How much of the glow stays in the clear core, so the mark does not sit in a dark square of its own.

rest_dark.doc: How strong the mark of a tab not in front is, dark theme: its colour mixed this far from the tab's ground toward the project's, and its glow times this.

rest_light.doc: The same, light theme: a lighter colour on a light ground loses contrast fast.

stack_tab._doc: The tabs over a cell that holds several terminals.

inset.doc: From the content's left and right edges to a tab's body: corner 8 + straight 4 + arc 8. Also the terminal text's inset.

tentative.why: At 16 the arc's foot meets the end of the corner and the two read as one S.

reverse_arc_radius.doc: The arcs that join the current tab's foot to the content.

overlap_below.doc: How far the current tab's fill runs past its foot, to cover the strip's line.

close_button.doc: Windows: each tab's close button at its right end, after the glyph (task 1582): the window tab's `close`. Its place is kept in every tab whether or not it is showing, so a tab does not change width when the pointer comes over it. macOS puts it at the left end, over the name, only while the pointer is on the tab, drawn as the system's own tabs draw theirs (`PolterCloseCircle`, task 1642), and keeps no place for it: a macOS tab is this and `close_gap` narrower, which `tools/control-room-hosts-agree.py` checks.

close_gap.doc: Windows: between a tab's glyph and its close button. Not on macOS (see `close_button`).

scroll_fade.doc: How wide the fade is at an end of the tabs when more of them are scrolled out of sight that way (task 1582, in place of the `more` menu).

trailing.doc: From the status at the right end of the strip to the strip's right edge. In a supervisor's frame this is measured inside the border, like `inset`.

status_gap.doc: The least between the plus and the status at the right end.

nominal_cell_width.doc: How wide one character of a tab's name is taken to be where there is no font to measure with: what the two hosts are held to one answer by. A wide character is two.

min_width.doc: The narrowest a tab ever is: one whose name wants less is widened to it (task 1675: a tab named `~` was barely wider than its close button, and a drag meant to move it closed it), and when the tabs do not fit they are squeezed to it and no further, then scroll sideways (task 1582; they used to go behind a `more` menu). 104 is the design's eight-letter tab: at that a name keeps seven characters and its ellipsis.

tentative.why: 68 is the design's three-letter tab (padding 12 + three cells + gap 8 + glyph 14 + padding 12): more tabs stay on the strip, and each is one letter and an ellipsis. The design draws no squeezed strip; where squeezing stops has not been ruled on.

quota._doc: The allowance block at the bottom of the list: a hairline, then one opened-out part for each account at or past the limit line, then the one line. 38.5 high on an ordinary day, 88.5 with one account close, 112.5 with one used up and a way out named.

separator_space_below.doc: Under the hairline that closes the list above.

line_height.doc: The one line: the label at the left, each account and its number at the right.

entry_gap.doc: Between two accounts in the one line.

label_gap.doc: The least between the label and the accounts.

alert_title_height.doc: Which account and which window and how much, and at the right when it comes back.

alert_glyph_gap.doc: Between the triangle and the words, when it is all gone.

bar_min_fill.doc: The least of the bar that is filled, so that a filled end is always a round one.

note_line_height.doc: The way out, under the bar of an account that is used up.

status._doc: The four status glyphs and how they move. Nothing moves under Reduce Motion.

waiting_pulse_period.doc: Only the one that has waited longest pulses.

problem_shake_distance.doc: Left and right, once, on entering the state.

working_spin_steps.doc: It steps; it does not turn smoothly.

working_spoke_width.doc: One of the spinner's short lines, on the artboard.

working_spoke_inset.doc: From the artboard's edge to a line's outer end.

working_spoke_min_opacity.doc: The faintest line; the brightest is 1 and the rest step up to it.

done_unseen_dot.doc: The dot's diameter on the artboard: a size smaller than the other glyphs.

elsewhere._doc: A terminal that is being shown somewhere else: the last frame it drew here, frosted, under the sentence that says where it went. The whole of it is one button.

blur.doc: How far the kept frame is blurred, as the sigma of a Gaussian in that frame's own pixels: enough that no word of it can be read.

veil.doc: How much of the terminal's ground is laid over the whole blurred frame. At 0.65 the frame can still be told for the screen it was (the supervisor, on build-18: at 0.86 it was "a flat colour and a line of words" again). The words are not kept readable by this; `shade` does that.

tentative.why: The user has seen neither on a real terminal; 0.86 is where the veil alone keeps the words at 4.5:1 and the frame is a faint shadow.

shade.doc: How much more of the terminal's ground there is behind the two lines of words, at the corners of their box -- where there is least of it under them. With the veil, 0.867 of the ground is under the words there: both lines keep 4.5:1 over any frame at all, white or black, in both themes. It is more than this at the middle and less everywhere further out: it has no flat part and no edge.

shade_spread.doc: How fast the shade falls away from its middle: the sigma of a Gaussian, as a fraction of the shade's radius. At the radius it is gone.

shade_words_within.doc: The shade's radius each way is at least the words' half-width (half-height) divided by this, and at least half the place's shorter side: so the corners of the words' box are never further out than 0.37 of the radius, where 0.65 of the middle's amount is left (the supervisor, on build-19: it read as a plate with an edge; it should read as the middle being a little deeper).

frame_longest_side.doc: The frame is kept no larger than this on its longer side, in pixels: it is only ever shown blurred.

selection._doc: The selected row of the group list and the selected window tab: a chip at rest, glass while it slides.

edge_band.doc: The width of the faint band just inside the chip's edge.

spring_damping.doc: Below 1, so it overshoots (about 4%) and settles.

tentative.why: Whether the chip overshoots at all has not been ruled on; 1 is critically damped.

lift_in.doc: How long the chip takes to lift when it starts to move.

lift_scale_window_tab.doc: The window tab's chip is the system's own piece of glass; this is how much of it the slide adds while it is in the air.

lift_lands_with_remaining.doc: The chip starts back down when this much of the way is still to go.

settled_within.doc: The slide is over once it stays this close to its end, as a fraction of the way: 0.41 s with the period and damping above; the design says about 0.45.

slide_samples_per_second.doc: The window tab's slide is handed to the system written out as this many positions a second.

glass_at_rest.doc: Whether the row's chip is the system's glass while it sits still. Off: at rest it is a plain bright piece with nothing live behind it, and the glass is only there for the slide.

tentative.why: Glass that sits still is recomposited whenever what is behind it changes; the one measurement of glass over a scrolling terminal found a cost in full screen. The user has not ruled.

stretch_along.doc: At most, with speed, along the direction of travel.

centre_zoom.doc: The middle of the chip while lifted.

refraction_shown.doc: Whether the chip's edge bends what is under it while it slides. It is the system's glass that bends it, where the system has one (macOS 26); nothing here moves pixels itself.

tentative.why: The other candidate keeps the lift and the slide and drops the refraction. What the system's glass looks like over the rows has not been seen in a window.

seen_after.doc: How long a row stays selected, with the control room in front, before its group counts as seen.

tentative.why: 0 marks it seen the moment it is selected, so arrowing past a row would clear it.

refraction_strength_rest.doc: A fraction of the band's width; strongest at the edge, falling off as the square.

highlight._doc: `terminal_highlight` (task 1689): the lit pane's edge, the card over it, the other panes' scrim, and the breathing that the edge, the card's ring and the lit terminal's tab share.

breath_period.doc: One breath, in and out: design A's glow, which the user asked for on B's edge, the card's ring and the tab.

breath_low.doc: The breathing's opacity at its faintest, as a fraction of the accent.

tentative.why: The design gives the period and not the depth; nobody has watched it breathe yet.

breath_high.doc: At its strongest. With reduce motion on it rests here and does not breathe.

edge.doc: Design B's edge round the lit pane, drawn this far outside it.

ring_a.doc: Design A's edge, for a pane too small for the card.

glow_a.doc: Design A's glow round that edge, as a blur radius.

card_min_pane_width.doc: A pane narrower than this gets design A instead of the card.

card_ring.doc: The accent ring round the card's own edge, which breathes with the pane's.

card_ring_alpha.doc: How much accent is in it at the top of a breath.

card_center_y.doc: The card's centre, as a fraction of the pane's height from its top.

label_size.doc: The caller's label, in the accent, weight 700.

fade_out.doc: How long it takes to go when the time is up.

tab_dot.doc: The accent dot before the lit terminal's tab's name.

tab_ground.doc: How much accent the lit terminal's tab -- window tab or stack tab -- is filled with at the top of a breath.

tab_edge.doc: The accent edge round that tab.

perf_card._doc: One terminal's card on the performance page (task 2015): head, body, foot, one grid for every card and every state, so nothing moves with what is in it.

head.doc: The name, the role, the badge.

gap.doc: Between head and body, and body and foot.

body.doc: The dial and the four rows beside it.

foot.doc: CPU and processes at the left, the time it has run at the right.

dial_gap.doc: From the dial to the rows: the rows' left edge is the card's one alignment line.

row1.doc: Use: the value at `font_value`, then the rest.

row3.doc: State, in six to eight characters.

dial_open_degrees.doc: How far round the arc goes; the gap is at the bottom.

dial_cap_top.doc: From the dial's top to the words in the arc's gap.

dial_radius.doc: The arc's radius, to the middle of its stroke, in the `dial` square.

dial_tick_inner.doc: A warn line's tick, from the dial's centre: from here.

dial_start_degrees.doc: Where the arc starts, clockwise from three o'clock; it runs `dial_open_degrees` from there.

curve_dash.doc: The dashed line at the kill line's height over the curve: a dash, then `curve_gap`.

font_big.doc: L1: the number in the dial.

font_value.doc: L2: the value in row 1. Everything else is L3, `font.body`.

badge_height.doc: The level badge at the head's right end.

between.doc: Between two cards, across and down. As many to a row as fit the page's width; the width never stretches.

perf_grid._doc: The history grid at the top of the performance page: one row per terminal, a cell per half hour (24 hours) or per four hours (7 days).

day_group.doc: 7 days: six cells to a day, a group.

group_gap.doc: 7 days: what a group adds to `cell_gap` before the next. 24 hours is not grouped.

label_width.doc: The terminal's name before its row.

head_height.doc: The title, the subtitle and the legend.

rows_top.doc: From the head to the first row.

axis_gap.doc: From the last row to the times under it.

tip_radius.doc: A cell's hover, drawn to the cell's left.

tip_offset.doc: From the hover's right edge to the cell.

perf_page._doc: The performance page as a whole (task 2015).

padding.doc: Round the page, inside the right column.

summary_pad_y.doc: Inside the box with the machine line and the grid, top and bottom.

summary_layer_gap.doc: In that box, between the machine line and the grid.

machine_height.doc: The machine line: memory, swap, pressure, the group's count, the 24-hour/7-day switch.

seg_rule.doc: The line under the one chosen.

cards_title_top.doc: From the box to the line over the cards.

cards_title_inset.doc: The line over the cards, in from their left and right edges.

cards_top.doc: From that line to the first row of cards.

task_page._doc: The task page (task 2015 Q9/Q10): the group's goal, a table of its tasks, the open one's detail, the closed ones folded, the keys at the foot.

pad_x.doc: Round the page, left and right.

goal_height.doc: The group's goal, the line at the top.

col_owner.doc: In the terminal's face. The title takes what is left.

col_idle.doc: How long since it moved, to the right.

closed_rule_gap.doc: From those words to the line after them.

detail_radius_mac.doc: The open task's ground on macOS.

detail_radius_windows.doc: The same on Windows, as the panels there are rounder by less.

detail_pad_left.doc: Lines the detail up with the title column.

detail_left_width.doc: The task and its log; the group's messages take the rest.

heading_rule_gap.doc: From a heading to the line after it.

log_track.doc: The track between the time and who.

log_track_x.doc: The track's line, from the column's left.

log_dot_top.doc: From the row's top to the dot's.

log_gap_row.doc: "18 minutes later": the track is dashed through it.

said_head_gap.doc: Between a message's time and who sent it.

hints_gap.doc: Between one key and its words and the next.

key_font.doc: The key, in the terminal's face.

key_gap.doc: From a key to its words.

selection_tint.doc: How much white the chip mixes in, at rest.

selection_edge.doc: The band inside the edge: darker when negative, lighter when positive.

selection_shadow_blur.doc: As the design's animation takes it; its still pictures use about twice this as a CSS blur.

selection_halo_blur.doc: A second shadow with no offset.

window_base.doc: The window's ground. The design lays two faint blooms over it.

attention.doc: Blue, something for you: the glyph of waiting and of done-and-unseen.

attention_text.doc: The same blue as a word or a number.

problem.doc: Red, something is wrong: the glyph.

problem_text.doc: The same red as a word or a number. See `text_on` for where the word is not red.

side_panel_highlight.doc: A hairline along the top edge.

supervisor_edge_focused.doc: Light: the outer edge darkens. Dark: a ring is added just inside it.

pane_blue.doc: A blue pane's dot: on its tab, on its stack tab, as its edge when panes wear no frames, in the menu.

pane_blue_badge.doc: The ground of a blue pane's badge at the left of its title. Dark grounds are light, with a dark word.

pane_blue_badge_text.doc: The mark and the word on a blue badge.

pane_purple.doc: A purple pane's dot: on its tab, on its stack tab, as its edge when panes wear no frames, in the menu. A supervisor given no colour is shown in this; on light it is the app icon's own (`images/Polter.icon/icon.json`).

pane_purple_badge.doc: The ground of a purple pane's badge at the left of its title. Dark grounds are light, with a dark word.

pane_purple_badge_text.doc: The mark and the word on a purple badge.

pane_pink.doc: A pink pane's dot: on its tab, on its stack tab, as its edge when panes wear no frames, in the menu.

pane_pink_badge.doc: The ground of a pink pane's badge at the left of its title. Dark grounds are light, with a dark word.

pane_pink_badge_text.doc: The mark and the word on a pink badge.

pane_red.doc: A red pane's dot: on its tab, on its stack tab, as its edge when panes wear no frames, in the menu.

pane_red_badge.doc: The ground of a red pane's badge at the left of its title. Dark grounds are light, with a dark word.

pane_red_badge_text.doc: The mark and the word on a red badge.

pane_orange.doc: A orange pane's dot: on its tab, on its stack tab, as its edge when panes wear no frames, in the menu.

pane_orange_badge.doc: The ground of a orange pane's badge at the left of its title. Dark grounds are light, with a dark word.

pane_orange_badge_text.doc: The mark and the word on a orange badge.

pane_yellow.doc: A yellow pane's dot: on its tab, on its stack tab, as its edge when panes wear no frames, in the menu.

pane_yellow_badge.doc: The ground of a yellow pane's badge at the left of its title. Dark grounds are light, with a dark word.

pane_yellow_badge_text.doc: The mark and the word on a yellow badge.

pane_green.doc: A green pane's dot: on its tab, on its stack tab, as its edge when panes wear no frames, in the menu.

pane_green_badge.doc: The ground of a green pane's badge at the left of its title. Dark grounds are light, with a dark word.

pane_green_badge_text.doc: The mark and the word on a green badge.

pane_teal.doc: A teal pane's dot: on its tab, on its stack tab, as its edge when panes wear no frames, in the menu.

pane_teal_badge.doc: The ground of a teal pane's badge at the left of its title. Dark grounds are light, with a dark word.

pane_teal_badge_text.doc: The mark and the word on a teal badge.

pane_graphite.doc: A graphite pane's dot: on its tab, on its stack tab, as its edge when panes wear no frames, in the menu.

pane_graphite_badge.doc: The ground of a graphite pane's badge at the left of its title. Dark grounds are light, with a dark word.

pane_graphite_badge_text.doc: The mark and the word on a graphite badge.

surface_row.doc: Measured: an unselected row as it comes out over the panel. For contrast, not for painting.

surface_window_tab.doc: Measured: an unselected window tab on its track.

highlight_scrim.doc: Over every other pane of the lit terminal's window (task 1689).

highlight_card_edge.doc: The highlight card's hairline, inside its accent ring.

level_none.doc: Performance page, a level (`tone`) the core hands over: no reading -- an empty cell of the grid. Light: undesigned.

level_ok.doc: A grid cell that stayed under every line. Light: undesigned.

level_ok_arc.doc: The dial of a card under every line. Light: undesigned.

level_warn1.doc: The first warn line: the arc, the grid cell. Light: undesigned.

level_warn1_text.doc: Words at that level: rows 2 and 3, the badge. Light: undesigned.

level_warn1_edge.doc: The card's edge and the badge's. Light: undesigned.

level_warn2.doc: The second warn line. Light: undesigned.

level_warn3.doc: The design draws two warn lines; a third and a fourth are drawn as the second. Here, not in a host, so no host decides it.

level_withheld.doc: The kill line counted on a terminal that may not be stopped: drawn as the second warn line, never the red of a stop.

level_killed.doc: Stopped at its kill line. Light: `problem`'s.

perf_dial_track.doc: The dial's track under the arc. Light: undesigned.

perf_curve.doc: The last minutes' curve in row 4. Light: undesigned.

perf_card.doc: A card's ground, and the box with the grid. Light: undesigned.

perf_tip.doc: A grid cell's hover, to its left. Light: undesigned.

surface_perf_card.doc: Measured: a card's ground as it comes out over the page (ui-v4 metrics.md). For the contrast report; a host draws `perf_card`. Light: undesigned.

task_queued.doc: The six task glyphs (`strings.task_symbol`). Queued: as `text_tertiary`.

task_done.doc: Done, waiting to be closed: as `text_secondary`.

task_symbol._doc: The six task glyphs, by the system symbol macOS draws; Windows draws the same shape by name (`glyph.rs`), at `side.glyph`.

symbol._doc: The system symbols the glyphs are. Working is the system's progress spinner, which has no symbol name. `held` is the supervisor's ruling (the design says only `a pause glyph`).

_doc: Which colour a status word is written in, by the surface it sits on.
Dark red text does not reach 4.5 on the lighter dark surfaces, and lightening the red makes it
another colour. So there the word is written in the main text colour and the red is left to the
glyph and the minutes. That is the whole of this table, and the hosts read it rather than decide.

tentative.why: The other candidate accepts a contrast of about 3. The user has not ruled.

_doc: What is drawn on what, for the contrast report (`gen-control-room-look.py --contrast`).
`text` needs 4.5, `large` (20 pt bold) and `glyph` need 3. `problem_word` is the status word
